crime: Her cell was the solo one; her friend's was next door, a stone wall between them. After the night lock, they knocked each other goodnight through the shared wall — two taps and two knocked back. Nightly, for months.
Her friend began spending free evenings in another girl's cell down the corridor — slipped in when no guard was looking, back just before the lock. She knocked goodnight; no knock came back.
Just before the lock that evening, her friend stepped out of the other girl's cell and tapped the double-knock on that cell's door bars. She watched from her own door.

The next evening — her friend at the other girl's cell, her friend's cellmate in the lounge — she slipped into her friend's empty cell and struck one blow into the shared wall, at the spot where the goodnight was always knocked. She stepped out; a girl passing the cells saw her leave.

The night lock. Her friend at the bunk, hand to the wall at the old goodnight spot — one knock. The blow fell out of the wall into the friend's chest at full force; the friend dropped at the head of the bunk. The cellmate, in the dark, heard one knock, one heavy blow, the fall.
Morning unlock: her friend lay dead beneath the goodnight spot. A single crushing blow to the chest, and nothing in the cell could account for it. The door had been locked from the outside all night.

The blow was past any bare hand's force; the cellmate cleared. The cell locked from the outside, nothing inside to swing — a blow left waiting. The heard order, knock then blow then fall — the blow met the friend at her own knock.

The wall tested ordinary under every later touch — a lodged blow spends itself in one landing; the unmarked wall was the spent weapon. Lodging is done by hand, in person; she was seen stepping out of the friend's empty cell that evening. The blow had waited at the spot where the friend knocked goodnight to her.
fields.epitaph: She threw the first blow at every leaving. The only one that ever came back for her was her own.
execution: A post rose on the execution stand. She was bound to it upright, one arm left free; before the free hand, a strike-plate.
Behind the plate, a heavy iron arm was drawn back on a spring, its catch tied to the plate.
Beside the catch, a slow clockwork of gears was walking it loose on its own, tooth by tooth.
She struck the plate. The catch freed, and the drawn arm swung through where she stood and took her across the chest.

magic.name: Forefist
magic.text: When she strikes a thing, the blow lodges where her fist landed. The first to disturb that spot takes the full force of the blow, and the thing is ordinary again.
